answer: Remote hardware attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to run inside a certified secure enclave. Anchoring identity in silicon as solid as basalt blocks virtual cloning, forcing attackers to buy scarce physical chips per node. Enclaves embed a cryptographic pigment into outbound attestations, ensuring even an identity as light as a sparrow incurs real hardware costs. However, this relies on centralized chipmaker root keys and remains vulnerable to side-channel exploits.
